rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the addressees to be Thamud; a reported alternative takes them as the most wretched one, understood collectively, compatible with the plural watering reference.
rows.anchor: أي لثمود أو لأشقاها على ما قيل بناءً أن المراد به جمع ولا يأباه وسقياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is Salih; calling him by his office signals that obedience to him is obligatory and highlights their extreme insolence.
rows.anchor: هو صالح عليه السلام وعبر عنه بعنوان الرسالة إيذاناً بوجوب طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqat Allah is accusative as a warning; Makkī explains the conditions for the construction, which need not involve repeating the warning.
rows.anchor: وهو نصب على التحذير وشرطه ليس تكرير المحذر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning can be expanded as beware slaughtering God's she-camel, though the omitted complement need not appear in the wording.
rows.anchor: والكلام على حذف مضاف أي احذروا عقر ناقة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggested estimate make much of or cling to God's she-camel is rejected as unsound.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون التقدير عظموا أو الزموا ناقة الله وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must leave her watering turn undisturbed, neither preventing her from it nor appropriating it for themselves.
rows.anchor: فلا تتعرضوا بمنعها عنها في نوبتها ولا تستأثروا بها عليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes the conjunction mean leave God's she-camel together with her watering and do not separate them; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل الواو للمعية والمراد ذروا ناقة الله مع سقياها ولا تحولوا بينهما وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī reads Naqat Allah in the nominative, understood as directing their concern to the she-camel and her watering, so they do not slaughter her or monopolize the water.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ناقة الله بالرفع فقيل أي همكم ناقة الله وسقياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied his warning about punishment; the denial may target an unstated prediction or the report implicit in the warning.
rows.anchor: أي في وعيده إياهم كما حكي عنه بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound alternative is that Salih reported God's command about the she-camel and watering, and they denied that divine report.
rows.anchor: كما يؤذن بذلك التعبير عنه عليه السلام بعنوان الرسالة ومآل ذلك أنه قال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqaruha means they slaughtered or killed her; the plural pronoun refers to the worst one, expressed collectively because everyone approved his act.
rows.anchor: أي فنحروها أو فقتلوها وضمير الجمع للأشقى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they did not hamstring her until their young and old, men and women, had followed and consented.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة بلغنا أنه لم يعقرها حتى تابعه صغيرهم وكبيرهم وذكرهم وأنثاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord enveloped them in punishment; the repeated form is analyzed as faʿfal and the phrase as covering or applying something over another.
rows.anchor: فأطبق عليهم العذاب وقالوا دمدم عليه القبر أي أطبقه وهو مما تكرر فيه الفاء

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs glosses the expression as completing the punishment against them.
rows.anchor: وقال في «القاموس » معناه أتم العذاب عليهم

rows.speaker: مؤرج
rows.claim: Muʾarrij defines damdama as destruction that exterminates completely.
rows.anchor: وقال مؤرج الدمدمة إهلاك باستئصال

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ glosses damdama as pressing something to the earth and crushing it.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح دمدمت الشيء ألزقته بالأرض وطحطحته

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads fa-dahdama, inserting hāʾ between the dāls, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير فدهدم بهاء بين الدالين والمعنى كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment came because of their sin; stating the cause despite the preceding fa warns every sinner about sin's consequence.
rows.anchor: بسبب ذنبهم المحكي والتصريح بذلك مع دلالة الفاء عليه للإنذار بعاقبة الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to the implied punishment, God made its effects equal among them so none escaped, young or old.
rows.anchor: الضمير للدمدمة المفهومة من دمدم أي فجعل الدمدمة سواء بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it refers to Thamud as a tribe, with feminine agreement as in ṭaghwāhā and ashqāhā; none escaped.
rows.anchor: أو هو لثمود والتأنيث باعتبار القبيلة كما في طغواها وأشقاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God levelled them with the ground.
rows.anchor: أو فسواها بالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra has twenty-one verses; most call it Meccan, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭalḥa calls it Medinan, and another view makes some Meccan and some Medinan.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف في أنها إحدى وعشرون آية واختلف في مكيتها ومدنيتها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the sūra was revealed concerning Abū Bakr; sound chains from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others report this.
rows.anchor: فالجمهور على أنها نزلت في شأن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه وروي ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says it concerned Abū al-Daḥdāḥ, who gave orphans a palm tree he bought from a hypocritical neighbor after fruit fell into their yard, in exchange for the promised palm in Paradise; the Prophet approved. Ibn ʿAbbās's report through Ibn Abī Ḥātim is weak according to al-Suyūṭī.
rows.anchor: قال السدي أنها نزلت في أبي الدحداح الأنصاري وذلك أنه كان في دار منافق نخلة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say the passage about the most God-fearing being kept from Hell was revealed about Abū Bakr; some claim consensus, while some Shiʿites assign it to ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن قوله تعالى فيها وسيجنبها الأتقى الخ نزل في أبي بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior sūra spoke of success; this one details traits leading to success or loss, then illustrates both outcomes.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبلها قد أفلح الخ ذكر سبحانه فيها من الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night may cover the sun, the day, or everything darkness veils; in each reading the oath is by the whole night.
rows.anchor: أي حين يغشى الشمس كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexed verbal noun means all your endeavors, collective in sense, which accounts for the plural predicate shattā.
rows.anchor: فإن المصدر المضاف يفيد العموم فيكون جمعاً معنى ولذا أخبر عنه بجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively shattā is a feminine verbal noun, a predicate with an implied dhū, an adjective meaning scattered, or the very notion of separation for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن لا يعتبر سعيكم في معنى الجمع ويكون شتى مصدراً مؤنثاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different endeavors differ in their recompense.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتفرق المساعي اختلافها في الجزاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, as transmitted by al-Ṭabarī, takes this sentence as the answer to the oath; al-Alūsī also allows an unstated answer.
rows.anchor: كما أخرجه ابن جرير عن قتادة وجوز أن يكون الجواب مقدراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This section explains how endeavors differ in outcome; the alternative that they differ as pursuits of night, day, male, or female is judged remote and awkward.
rows.anchor: تفصيل مبين لتفرقها واختلافها في ذلك وجوز أن يراد باختلافها كون البعض طالباً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of giving is to give wealth.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالإعطاء بذل المال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets giving as spending one's wealth in God's cause.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد المراد إنفاق ماله في سبيل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets giving as paying God's due, apparently the financial dues.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة المعنى أعطى حق الله تعالى وظاهره الحقوق المالية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses God-consciousness as fearing God.
rows.anchor: أي واتق الله عز وجل كما قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains it as avoiding what God forbade and His inviolable limits.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه قول قتادة واتقى ما نهى عنه وفي رواية محارم الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets this as refraining from miserliness, a gloss al-Alūsī dismisses.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد واتقي البخل وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and others, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, identify al-ḥusnā as the best word, there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وغيره وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes al-ḥusnā as whatever signifies truth, centrally including the declaration of divine unity.
rows.anchor: أو هي ما دلت على حق كما قال بعضهم وتدخل كلمة التوحيد دخولاً أولياً

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and a group identify al-ḥusnā as the best religion, Islam.
rows.anchor: وهي ملة الإسلام وقال عكرمة وجماعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says al-ḥusnā is reward returned in this world with increase.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أيضاً هي المثوبة بالخلف في الدنيا مع المضاعفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies al-ḥusnā as Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation is reward in general.
rows.anchor: وقيل المثوبة مطلقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī prefers giving as financial worship, taqwā as all other worship through good acts and avoiding sins, and belief in al-ḥusnā as tawḥīd or comprehensive faith; together they cover all endeavors.
rows.anchor: ويترجح عندي أن الإعطاء إشارة إلى العبادة المالية والاتفاء إشارة إلى ما يشمل سائر

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticates a report: Abū Bakr's father urged him to free strong men who could defend him instead of weak slaves; Abū Bakr replied that he sought what he sought, and the passage from 92:5 to 92:19 was revealed.
rows.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وصححه عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه قال قال أبو قحافة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya b. Khalaf for a cloak and ten awāq and freed him; verses 92:1–4 were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال أن أبا بكر اشترى بلالاً من أمية بن خلف ببردة وعشرة أواق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī notes the same explanation of the order applies if the revelation occasion is Abū al-Daḥdāḥ.
rows.anchor: وكذا على القول بأنها نزلت في أبي الدحداح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith follows taqwā as a special after a general, and is delayed despite its importance to preserve the verse ending.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإيمان أمراً معتنى به في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes giving obedience, taqwā avoidance of sin, and al-ḥusnā the word of truth such as tawḥīd; al-Alūsī objects that giving conventionally concerns money, especially opposite withholding, and the order remains unexplained.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد أعطي الطاعة واتتقي المعصية وصدق بالكلمة الدالة على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says obedience includes listening to learn tawḥīd and taqwā includes avoiding idolatry, both preceding faith; al-Alūsī rejects it.
rows.anchor: وقيل آخر لأن من جملة إعطاء الطاعة الإصغاء لتعلم كلمة التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will ready him for a disposition leading to ease and comfort, such as entering Paradise and its preliminaries; this recalls readying a horse for riding by saddling and bridling it.
rows.anchor: فسنهيئه للخصلة التي تؤدي إلى يسر وراحة كدخول الجنة ومباديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the outcome al-yusrā is explained as explicit metaphor, metonymy, or figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: ووصفها باليسرى إما على الاستعارة المصرحة أو المجاز المرسل أو التجوز في الإسناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He withholds his wealth instead of spending it in good causes.
rows.anchor: بما له فلم يبذله في سبيل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported alternative says he withholds obedience to what he was commanded; al-Alūsī dismisses it.
rows.anchor: وقيل أي بخل بفعل ما أمر به وفيه ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He behaves as though he has no need of God or what is with Him, and so does not fear Him.
rows.anchor: وزهد فيما عنده عز وجل كأنه مستغن عنه سبحانه فلم يتقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively he is satisfied with worldly desires instead of afterlife bliss, fitting the contrast with God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: أو استغنى بشهوات الدنيا عن نعيم العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison to al-ḥusnā follows the interpretations already given for verse 6.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالحسنى فيه ما مر في الأقوال قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of denial, al-ḥusnā, has the interpretations already discussed for verse 6.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالحسنى فيه ما مر في الأقوال قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast describes withholding wealth from good, disdain for God's provision or preference for worldly pleasure, and denial of al-ḥusnā; the alternative gloss of withholding commanded acts is dismissed.
rows.anchor: بما له فلم يبذله في سبيل الخير وقيل أي بخل بفعل ما أمر به وفيه ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God readies him for a disposition leading to hardship, such as entering Hell and its preliminaries; al-ʿusrā is formed analogously to al-yusrā.
rows.anchor: أي للخصلة المؤدية إلى العسر والشدة كدخول النار ومباديه ووصفها بالعسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though taysīr derives from ease, here it means preparing and readying for what brings ease or hardship.
rows.anchor: وأصل التيسير من اليسر بمعنى السهولة لكن أريد التهيئة والإعداد للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle may add emphasis or indicate the magnitude and delayed realization of the promised next-world recompense.
rows.anchor: والسين في سنيسره قيل للتأكيد وقيل للدلالة على أن لحزاء الموعود معظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of withholding, self-sufficiency, and denial follows the explanation already given.
rows.anchor: وتقديم البخل فالاستغناء فالتكذيب يعلم وجهه مما تقدم

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says giving and withholding head the two clauses, though lower in rank than what follows, because each is foundational to the ensuing faith and piety or denial and self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل مع أن كلا منهما أدنى رتبة مما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the outcomes obedience: God grants لطف and success toward obedience for the giver, and withdraws enabling graces so obedience becomes hardest for the miser, related to 6:125.
rows.anchor: وقيل التيسير أولاً بمعنى اللطف وثانياً بمعنى الخذلان واليسرى والعسرى الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā as the paths to Paradise and Hell and taysīr as guidance, a promise and threat concerning the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد باليسرى طريق الجنة وبالعسرى طريق النار وبالتيسير في الموضعين معنى الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī considers it sound and near that taysīr means preparation and the outcomes are obedience and disobedience together with their good or blameworthy dispositions.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالتيسير التهيئة والإعداد واليسرى والعسرى الطاعة والمعصية ومباديهما

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: In a report from ʿAlī, the Prophet says each person's seats in Paradise and Hell are written; when asked whether to rely on this, he commands action, saying each is made easy for the deeds suited to their created end, and recites 92:5–7.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's command to work means fulfill servanthood and the purpose of creation, while leaving hidden matters of divine lordship to God.
rows.anchor: عليكم بشأن العبودية وما خلقتم لأجله وأمرتم به وكلوا أمور الربوبية المغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite specific reported occasions, the two descriptions apply generally because the wording is general; each person named is an included example.
rows.anchor: وان كان السبب خاصاً إذ العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب نعم هو قطعي الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the giver as Abū Bakr and the miser as Umayya b. Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقيل من أعطى أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه ومن بخل أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to identify them as Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb; al-Alūsī questions this because Abū Sufyān later became a strong Muslim according to Sunnis.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الأول أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه والثاني أبو سفيان بن حرب

rows.speaker: الطستي
rows.claim: In al-Ṭustī's narration from Ibn ʿAbbās, the miser passage was revealed about Abū Jahl; al-Alūsī treats all named identities as instances of the general wording.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية الطستي عنه أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening may be a negative statement, his wealth will not avail him, or an interrogative, what can his wealth avail him?
rows.anchor: أي ولا يغنى عنه على أن ما نافية أو أي شيء يغنى عنه ماله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses taraddā as perishing.
rows.anchor: أي هلك تفعل من الردي وهو الهلاك قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss is falling into the grave pit.
rows.anchor: وقيل تردي في حفرة القبر

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Qatāda and Abū Ṣāliḥ say it means falling into Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح تردي في جهنم أي سقط

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take taraddā from the shroud, a metaphor for his death and destruction.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم ترى باكفانه من الرداء وهو كناية عن موته وهلاكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This resumes and confirms what precedes: under His wise decree, having created people for worship, God guides them to truth or clarifies guidance and misguidance, which He has fully done.
rows.anchor: استئناف مقرر لما قبله أي إن علينا بموجب قضائنا المبني على الحكم البالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish the Muʿtazilite claim that guidance is something God is obligated to provide.
rows.anchor: فلا يتم الاستدلال بالآية على الوجوب عليه عز وجل بالمعنى الذي يزعمه المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view means guidance is entrusted to God alone, citing that the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; al-Alūsī objects that the implied verb entrusted makes the syntax unlikely.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد أن الهدى موكول علينا لا على غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss is that the path of guidance is upon God: whoever follows the clarified way arrives at Him, by analogy to the straight path being upon God; al-Alūsī likewise finds this attachment unlikely.
rows.anchor: ما قيل أن المراد ثم أن علينا طريقة الهدى على معنى أن من سلك الطريقة المبينة بالهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has complete disposal over both abodes and may do as He wills, including reward and punishment; alternatively, all they contain belongs to Him, so human guidance or error cannot benefit or harm Him.
rows.anchor: أي التصرف الكلي فيهما كيفما نشاء فنفعل فيهما ما نشاء من الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever is guided benefits himself, while whoever strays bears the loss himself.
rows.anchor: كما لا يضرنا ضلالكم فمن اهتدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ashqā refers to the unbeliever, more wretched than the sinner; the next verse clarifies this with denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: المراد به الكافر فإنه أشقى من الفاسق ويفصح بذلك وصفه بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denied the truth.
rows.anchor: أي بالحق { وتولى } وأعرض عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He turned away from obedience.
rows.anchor: أي بالحق { وتولى } وأعرض عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will keep the most God-fearing—those who intensely avoid unbelief and sins—far from Hell, not even approaching it.
rows.anchor: أي سيبعد عنها { الاتقى } المبالغ في اتقاء الكفر والمعاصي فلا يحوم حولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent restrictions seem to conflict: the first excludes sinful believers from Hell, while the second implies they are not kept away and so enter it.
rows.anchor: فالحصر السابق يقتضي أن لا يصلي المؤمن العاصي النار لأنه ليس داخلاً في عموم الأشقى

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munīr transmits from language scholars that ṣalā is especially severe exposure to heat, like pushing a sheep between layers of embers; sinners may enter or suffer lesser punishment without that torment, while the most God-fearing do not enter.
rows.anchor: فقد نقل ابن المنير عن أئمة اللغة أن الصلى أن يحفروا حفيرة فيجمعوا فيها جمراً كثيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the severe-torment interpretation, the first restriction denies only the most severe punishment to others, and the second does not require every less-pious person to enter or suffer it; they may receive lesser punishment.
rows.anchor: فيجوزو أن يدخلها ويعذب بها على وجهها عذاباً ليس بالأشد فلا مخالفة بين الحصرين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the restrictions rhetorical hyperbole in a comparison of exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers, not strict exclusions; al-Kashf praises this, but al-Alūsī notes its Muʿtazilite premise of eternal punishment for major sinners.
rows.anchor: قرر الزمخشري الاستشكال بأنه قد علم أن كل شقي بصلاها وكل تقي بجنيها

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the indefinite Hell in verse 15 could mean one level, so it need not say only unbelievers enter any Hell; al-Zamakhsharī objects that verse 17 then appears to keep all but the most pious from that level.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي إن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī may reject implication from the description, so verse 17 does not restrict exclusion to the most pious; those who reject such implication avoid most of the conflict.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لعل هذها القائل لا يقول بمفهوم الصفة ونحوها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet stated that only the wretched enter Hell; asked who they are, he replied they neither perform obedience nor avoid disobedience to God. Murjiʾites cite it, while Sunnis interpret sound reports alongside texts about punishment of major sinners.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal treats the elatives as ordinary descriptors, a wretched person and a pious person; Ṭarafa uses wāḥid to mean alone, but this does not solve the restriction problem for unbelievers, poor pious people, children, and the mentally ill.
rows.anchor: وقيل في الجواب أن المراد بالأشقى والاتقى الشقي والتقي وشاع أفعل في مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses wāḥid in the sense of alone, supporting the proposed non-elative reading.
rows.anchor: تمنى رجال أن أموت فإن أمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After considering alternatives, al-Alūsī favors al-Kashshāf's rhetorical reading if one accepts descriptive implication, despite rejecting eternal damnation for sinful believers.
rows.anchor: نستحسن إن قلت بالمفهوم ما استحسنه صاحب الكشف مما مر عن الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jannaba takes two objects: the pronoun is the second, while al-atqā is the first object and passive subject; the root often denotes distancing someone.
rows.anchor: وجنب يتعدى إلى مفعولين فالضمير ههنا المفعول الثاني والاتقى المفعول الأول

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that without an explicit object the verb means being kept from good; it derives from putting someone's side away and often means distancing.
rows.anchor: على ما قال الراغب أبعد عن الخير وأصلب جنبته كما قيل جعلته على جانب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives and spends his wealth.
rows.anchor: أي يعطيه ويصرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives seeking wealth that is pure and growing with God, without ostentation or reputation, or seeking purification from sins.
rows.anchor: طالباً أن يكون عند الله تعالى زاكياً نامياً لا يريد به رياء ولا سمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in yuʾtī.
rows.anchor: فالجملة نصب على الحال من ضمير يؤتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative parses make the clause a substitute for the relative clause, or the verb alone a substitute for the preceding verb; both are challenged because the relative clause has no case ending to follow and the verb's nominative is independently due to its being ungoverned.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون بدلاً من الصلة فلا محل لها من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replies allow follower status to mean same case when available or matching its presence or absence; calling an uninflected word a follower may be figurative due to resemblance, and a case may be intended even when independently licensed. Al-Sayyid ʿĪsā defines it as a second word that would be inflected if it were inflectable.
rows.anchor: وقيل إطلاق التابع على ذلك ونحوه من الحرف والفعل الغير المعرب مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies li-an before yatizakkā as the purpose of giving, deleting both lām and an; the verb may be raised or subjunctive, as in two transmitted readings of Ṭarafa's line.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون يتزكى بتقدير لأن يتزكى متعلقاً بيؤتي علة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On any parse, the wealth is spent in charitable and good causes.
rows.anchor: وأياً ما كان يدل الكلام على أن المراد بأيتائه صرفه في وجوه البر والخير

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī reads yazakkā, assimilating the tāʾ into the zāy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن علي بن الحسن بن علي
